purpose: Verify that one direct departure closure forces a 60-minute delay and that aircraft/crew continuity propagates the minimum necessary 20-minute delay to the next flight.
manual_checks: Validate reports the Scenario as valid.
Visualization shows one direct disruption exposure at A affecting WB2_F101.
The A 07:30-09:00 interval shows departure capacity 0 / departure closure.
Recovered WB2_F102 departs at 10:00 (+20 min) because AC1/C1 arrive B at 10:00.
WB2_F103 and the complete WB2_AC2/WB2_C2 rotation remain at original times.
No impossible aircraft or crew space-time jump appears.
Recovery contains exactly two DELAY actions.
design_notes: The disruption record and airport-interval closure are deliberately both present: disruption drives Workbench direct-exposure visualization, while the interval capacity/closure makes the restriction binding in the formal full-scope solver.
The closure is half-open [07:30,09:00), so WB2_F101_D60 departing exactly at 09:00 is the first feasible F101 option.
The canonical E1 aircraft minimum turn and crew minimum connection are both zero in the current test profiles. Therefore F101_D60 arriving B at 10:00 connects exactly to F102_D20 departing at 10:00.
Default flight delay cost is 1 per minute and cancellation is much more expensive, so the intended schedule cost is 60 + 20 = 80.
